items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: "I'll meet you in the morning, Jimmy says to me, we're gonna go down in the morning to get your cabaret card straightened out... and he said, 'Yeah man, I got a Buell fiddle that you can have'"

ctx.x: And, at that particular time, Frank Sinatra, as well as Sophie Tucker refused to work in New York in those big rooms unless they abolished that cabaret card business. And that made the police department mad, and they started going around raiding the clubs, and whoever had any kind of minor bust, you know, they were snatching their cards from them.

So naturally we had to look out for everything, so "I'll meet you in the morning, Jimmy says to me, we're gonna go down in the morning to get your cabaret card straightened out, you know, and reissue it to you because it had elapsed, and he said, "Yeah man, I got a Buell fiddle that you can have" -- and give me a bass. And he ended Allen Eager had given up getting me an apartment, and I was living there right on

West Broadway, and next morning, Jimmy comes by dutifully, and we go down to the license bureau, and sitting up there, the man says, "Oh yeah, Wilbur Ware -- have a seat." He says to me, "We'll get your card straightened out for you in a few minutes." So I'm sitting and sitting, and Jimmy said, "Well, what's the trouble?" and he says, "Oh, we're getting to it" and pretty soon here come two detectives. They called out to Brooklyn. And the come in and said, "Oh, here's that bass fiddle snatcher we been looking…
